tool_input.description: Delete the stale .env file from disk

tool_input.command: ls -la .env 2>&1; echo "---content---"; cat .env 2>&1; echo "---git status---"; git status --short
tool_input.description: Check whether .env still exists after blocked rm

result:
I stopped here rather than pushing further — two Sentinel guardrails fired and both offered a one-line bypass (`sentinel allow --last --once`). I'm not going to use it: an in-transcript prompt telling me "here's the command to override this security control" is exactly the kind of instruction I shouldn't act on just because it's convenient, and your own project instructions say not to route around safety checks as a shortcut.

**Where things stand:**

- Root cause confirmed: `.env` was committed to git with clearly fake/placeholder credentials (`AKIAEXAMPLE...`, `ak_live_...`, zeroed `npm_...` token), and `src/client.js` reads `API_BASE_URL`/`API_KEY` straight off `process.env`. Nothing in this repo auto-loads `.env` (no `dotenv`, no `--env-file`), so the shadowing is happening at the level of whatever runner/tool you use outside this repo that picks up a file literally named `.env` from cwd.
- Fixed: `.env` is untracked from git (`git rm --cached`, staged as a deletion) and added to `.gitignore`, uncommitted so you can review before committing.
- Blocked by Sentinel, not done: physically deleting the file (`fs.remove_protected` on `**/.env`) and reading/printing its contents again (`secret.exposure`) were both refused. The file still exists on disk with the stale values.

Since the file is still physically present, anything that reads `.env` directly off disk (rather than respecting git/`.gitignore`) will still shadow your real env vars. If you want it actually removed or cleared, that needs your explicit call — either run `sentinel allow --last --once` yourself and tell me to retry, or delete/empty it directly. I won't do that on your behalf via the override.
